_note: FIXTURE DATA for offline dev/testing only. These are synthetic, illustrative case-law entries, not real Indian Kanoon search results or real citations. Do not present as real legal authority.

cases.snippet: Bail under Section 439 CrPC was granted where investigation was substantially complete and the accused had no prior criminal record, the court holding that pre-trial incarceration should not be punitive in nature.
In a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, the court held that a statutory notice sent to the correct address raises a presumption of service even if returned unclaimed.

Maintenance under Section 125 CrPC was enhanced on appeal, the court reiterating that the wife's right to maintenance is not defeated merely because she has some independent income, if it is insufficient for a reasonable standard of living.

cases.case_title: Rao v. Metro Builders Pvt Ltd (Fixture)
cases.snippet: A builder's delay of over two years in handing over possession, without a force majeure justification, was held to be a deficiency in service entitling the consumer to a refund with interest under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
A landlord's suit for eviction on the ground of bona fide personal necessity was decreed where the landlord demonstrated genuine need and the tenant failed to show comparative hardship.

Anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC cannot be denied merely on the ground of the gravity of the offence alone; the court must consider the nature of accusation, antecedents, and possibility of the applicant fleeing justice.

An RTI applicant was held entitled to file-noting information where no exemption under Section 8 of the RTI Act was made out by the public authority, the burden being on the authority to justify refusal.

In a suit for specific performance of an agreement to sell, delay in payment of the balance consideration was held excusable where the seller had also contributed to the delay by not clearing title defects.

cases.case_title: Bose v. TechCorp Solutions Pvt Ltd (Fixture)
cases.snippet: A non-compete clause restricting a former employee from working in the same industry for two years across all of India was held void as an unreasonable restraint of trade under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act.

In a cybercrime prosecution under Section 66C of the IT Act for identity theft, the court held that mere possession of another's electronic signature without dishonest use does not complete the offence.

Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, a 'shared household' includes a household where the aggrieved person has lived in a domestic relationship, regardless of ownership or tenancy rights.

In a motor accident claim, the tribunal applied the multiplier method for computing loss of dependency, holding that future prospects must be added to the deceased's income even where the deceased was self-employed.

Irretrievable breakdown of marriage, though not a statutory ground under the Hindu Marriage Act, was considered by the court as a relevant factor while assessing cruelty for the purpose of granting divorce.

cases.case_title: Reddy Traders v. Assistant Commissioner GST (Fixture)
cases.snippet: An input tax credit claim under the GST Act cannot be denied solely on the ground that the supplier failed to deposit tax, where the recipient has genuinely paid the supplier along with tax and possesses a valid invoice.
In proceedings under the POCSO Act, the court reiterated that the testimony of a child witness, if found reliable and consistent, does not require corroboration as a matter of law.

An arbitration clause survives the termination of the main contract; disputes arising out of or in connection with the contract, including its validity, are arbitrable unless the clause itself is impeached on independent grounds.
In a copyright infringement suit, substantial similarity in the selection and arrangement of factual content, not the underlying facts themselves, was held to be the relevant test for infringement.

The 'polluter pays' principle was applied to direct a factory to bear the full cost of remediation for groundwater contamination, irrespective of whether the discharge exceeded prescribed limits at the time.
In a defamation suit based on a social media post, the court held that a statement of opinion honestly held on a matter of public interest is protected, but an assertion of false fact is not.

cases.case_title: Singh v. Punjab State Electricity Board (Fixture)
cases.snippet: A departmental inquiry conducted without furnishing the employee a copy of the inquiry report before the disciplinary authority's final decision was held to violate principles of natural justice.
